claim: `pinstart(adc_pin, $8_C600, %00_0111, 0)` does not configure the ADC. $8_C600 has %SSSSS (D[5:1]) = 0, so the smart pin stays off, and M[12:10] = %010, not the %100 the page itself requires (:13, :50). Internally clocked ADC is P_ADC_1X | P_ADC = $0011_8030 (M = %1000110000000 at D[20:8], %SSSSS = %11000). The same page's PASM literal `%0000_0000_000_100011_0000000_00_11000_0` (= $0011_8030) is right; the Spin2 call and its comment `%100011 in bits 17:12` (the field is D[20:15]) are not. The block compiles.
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/spin2-v55/spin2-v55-text.txt:1469 (P_ADC_1X), :1554 (P_ADC); engineering/ingestion/sources/silicon-doc/silicon-doc-text.txt:3731, :4420 (`WRPIN ##%100011_0000000_00_11000_0`)

claim: Pulse/cycle X halves are swapped. The base period is X[15:0] and the compare value X[31:16] (high while the counter, counting down from X[15:0], is above X[31:16]). `X=$0003_0002 ... 3-clock period` (:27) and `$0010_0008 ... 16-clock period, 50% duty` (:29, :74) and `pattern := $0003_0002 ' 3-clock period, high when > 2` (:85) put the compare value in the period half: $0003_0002 has period 2 and compare 3 (never high); the source's 0-0-1 example is X[15:0]=3, X[31:16]=2 (= $0002_0003), and 16 clocks at 50% is $0008_0010. `SHL x,#16 ' X[31:16] = 0 (continuous)` (:107-108) moves the width INTO the compare half and leaves a base period of 0 (65,536 clocks). The blocks compile.
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/silicon-doc/silicon-doc-text.txt:3970-3972, :3980; the page's own square_wave routine (:118-126) has the right order

claim: NCO-duty arithmetic cannot produce the stated duty. (1) `y_value := (duty_percent * $FFFFFFFF) / 100` (:62): $FFFFFFFF is -1 in Spin2, so 50 * -1 / 100 = 0 -- duty 0 for every percentage. (2) `y_value := MULDIV64(...) * ($FFFFFFFF / period)` (:76): $FFFFFFFF / period = -1 / 4,000,000 = 0, so y_value = 0. (3) `period := _clkfreq / 50` (:73) is 4,000,000 at 200 MHz, but X[15:0] is the base period (16 bits) and X[31:16] is the initial phase, so WXPIN(PWM_PIN, period) loads a phase. (4) PASM `MUL y_value, ##$28F5C29 ' x (2^32/100)` then `SHL y_value, #2` (:114-115): MUL is a 16x16 multiply of D[15:0] * S[15:0], so only $5C29 of the constant is used. All compile.
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/p2-instructions-csv/P2 Instructions v35 - Rev B_C Silicon - Sheet1.csv:161 (MUL: `D = unsigned (D[15:0] * S[15:0])`); engineering/ingestion/sources/silicon-doc/silicon-doc-text.txt:4021-4025 (NCO duty X[15:0] base period, X[31:16] -> Z[31:16])

claim: `receive_msb` calls `receive_byte` (which already does `SHR data,#24`, leaving the byte in D[7:0]), then `REV data` and `ZEROX data,#7`: REV moves the byte to D[31:24] and ZEROX #7 keeps only D[7:0], so the result is always 0. For MSB-first words the order is REV of the raw MSB-justified Z, then trim. The page's own Spin2 `receive_msb_first` (:97-102) has the right order (REV the raw RDPIN, then mask).
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/silicon-doc/silicon-doc-text.txt:4681 (`REV D` + `ZEROX D,#8` on the received word)

claim: In cog-mode DAT code a label's value is a COG address. `mov ptra, ##message` (11110:82), `mov ptra, ##buffer` (11111:80), `MOV ptra, #sine_table` (00010:130) and `MOV ptra, #breath_table` (00111:139) then use that cog address as a HUB pointer for RDBYTE/WRBYTE, so they read and write hub RAM near address 0, not the table or buffer (the hub address is `##@label`). `cmp count, #buffer_size wz` (11111:89) compares with the cog address of the `buffer_size` label, not the 256 stored there (register form: `cmp count, buffer_size wz`). `buffer long 0[256] ' 256-byte buffer` (:97) is 256 longs = 1,024 bytes of cog RAM. All compile.
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/spin2-v55/spin2-v55-text.txt:311, :320 (`#IncPins` is the cog address, `@IncPins` the hub address)

claim: `SETQ dividend_high` / `QDIV divisor, dividend_low`: QDIV divides {Q, D} by S, so D is the LOW dividend long and S the divisor; the example has them the other way round (divisor in D, dividend_low in S), dividing by dividend_low. Correct: `QDIV dividend_low, divisor`. (The `qdiv clkf, #10` lines in smart-pin-01101-a-rise-inc-dec-by-b.yaml and smart-pin-10010 / 10101 are in the right order.)
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/p2-instructions-csv/P2 Instructions v35 - Rev B_C Silicon - Sheet1.csv:260 (QDIV: `{SETQ value or 32'b0, D} / S`)

claim: The SMPS example routes `P_MINUS1_A | P_PLUS1_B` with smps_out = 20, i_sense = 19 and v_sense = 21, so input A is the CURRENT sense (pin 19) and input B the VOLTAGE feedback (pin 21). The mode's A input is the voltage detector (a low A starts a new cycle) and B the over-current detector (a high B truncates the cycle) -- as the page itself says at :10-13, :34-35. Roles are swapped. Also :39 `100kHz switching`: base 25 clocks x frame 256 at 250 MHz is 39 kHz.

claim: The barrier waits for '7 signals' with seven WAITATN. ATN is a single event FLAG (set by a strobe, cleared by POLLATN/WAITATN/JATN/JNATN); strobes from several cogs in the same clock are OR'd into one per-cog strobe and several strobes before a WAITATN set the same one bit. Waiting for seven separate events can hang. `MOV mask,#1` / `SHL mask, my_id` (:226-227) compute a mask that nothing uses, and `COGATN #%11111111` strobes the cog itself.

claim: `Monitor pins 7:0 for any change` reads `RDPIN last_state, #0` / `AND #$FF`, and `Sample all inputs` reads `RDPIN sample1, #0 ...#2`.
